references.text: Jesus sent out the twelve and instructed them not to take anything for the journey—no staff, bag, bread, money, or extra clothes. In [ref:Luk 9:3|Luke 9:3], we find the original sending that Jesus refers back to in 22:35.

When Jesus sent out the seventy, he said, 'Carry no moneybag, no bag, and no sandals' ([ref:Luk 10:4|Luke 10:4]). This is the second sending that Jesus reminds the disciples of, with nearly identical wording to 22:35.

In [ref:Matt 10:9-10|Matthew 10:9-10], Jesus gives similar instructions for the sending of the twelve: they are not to take gold, silver, copper, a bag, extra clothes, sandals, or a staff. This is Matthew's parallel to the sending command that Jesus refers back to.

In [ref:Mark 6:8-9|Mark 6:8-9], we find Mark's version of the instructions for the sending of the twelve, where they were not to take anything except a staff—no bread, bag, or money. Jesus refers to this experience in Luke 22:35.

Paul writes in [ref:Fil 4:19|Philippians 4:19] that God will supply all their needs according to his riches in Christ Jesus. This underscores the same principle that Jesus confirms in Luke 22:35: that God provides for those he sends out so that they lack nothing.

In [ref:Luk 22:36|Luke 22:36], Jesus follows up with a contrast: 'But now' they are to take a moneybag, a bag, and a sword. The new situation after Jesus' arrest and death will require a different approach than what they experienced during their first sending (v. 35).

Paul testifies in [ref:2 Kor 11:9|2 Corinthians 11:9] that he lacked nothing when he was in need, because the brothers from Macedonia provided for him. This reflects the principle from Luke 22:35 that God's servants are supported when they are sent out.
